handoff.reason: Case report of possible DHEA-induced mania — adverse-event signal, not efficacy evidence.

identity_notes: DHEA-in-humans evidence is heavily fragmented by indication (adrenal insufficiency, aging/well-being, depression, IVF/diminished ovarian reserve, SLE/rheumatic disease, sexual function) with no single population generalizable to the generic label. A major recurring applicability split: oral DHEA (the label material) shows little-to-no benefit for healthy-aging/well-being/sexual-function outcomes in the largest, best-controlled trials (e.g., PMID 17050889, 15996074, 19619146), while a separate and much larger evidence base concerns INTRAVAGINAL DHEA (prasterone/Intrarosa) for genitourinary syndrome of menopause — that route is NOT the oral supplement route and was excluded (not_this_route) throughout this screen (e.g., 18598765, 20459349, 25511551, 25968836, 26291918, 29164377, 30244783, 33307219, 36300276, 37130371, 37543737, 39250810, 41903372); reviewers should not let vaginal-DHEA trial volume leak into oral-supplement conclusions. Best-supported oral-DHEA signal in this retrieved scope is in primary/secondary adrenal insufficiency (bone density, some well-being subscales) and possibly diminished ovarian reserve/IVF adjuvant use (multiple meta-analyses, though these mix DHEA with other adjuvants such as CoQ10/testosterone/GH and the DHEA-specific primary-outcome signal is inconsistent, e.g. 39332623). Depression evidence (30124161, 32930419) is graded very-low-to-low quality by the reviews' own GRADE assessments. One retracted RCT (32451660) is included in the screened/kept counts for completeness but flagged integrity=retracted and excluded from the shortlist.
